newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal grants 13 gold exploration permits.
newsitem.headline: Senegal grants 13 gold exploration permits.

text.p: Senegal has granted 13 new gold exploration permits for eastern areas with proven reserves estimated at 30 tonnes, a government official said on Tuesday.
"The General Council of Mines has issued 13 gold exploration permits," director of mines Abdoulaye Dia told Reuters.
South Africa's Anglovaal, Canada's Etruscan Enterprises Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp, and Australia's Tarcoola had taken all 13 permits although 16 companies had applied, he said.
A recent study by Australian firm Paget Mining Co Ltd confirmed a proven reserve estimate of 30 tonnes of gold at Sabodala in eastern Senegal.

Prime Minister Habib Thiam has said Senegal would start gold production by 1998 and 40 gold exploration permits have been granted to companies including world league players such as Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields and South Africa's Anglo-American and Randgold.
"Three more permits will be issued for gold exploration," the director of mines said.
Senegal also has large marble reserves, estimated to be around 1.2 million tonnes, waiting to be tapped, officials said.
